messages:
alex: Hey team, escalating a support ticket from AcmeMaps. They see a sudden increase in 429s and huge tail latencies for requests routed to eu-west-1 starting ~2024-11-12T14:04:xx UTC. They say traffic is steady but errors spike when bursts hit. Logs attached below from their repro run.

alex: Repro steps they ran: curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" -d '{\"model\":\"gpt-open-16k\",\"prompt\":\"hello\"}' --parallel 50

alex: Sample response header when 429 occurs: 
  HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
  x-rate-limit-global: 0
  x-rate-limit-reset: 6
  x-region: eu-west-1
  x-request-queue-time-ms: 1450

alex: Customer says they saw queue times jump to 1.2s and then requests were retried and routed to us-west which added ~300-600ms, whole flow causing timeouts in their client. They also observed a lot of \"region_capacity_exhausted\" messages in our proxy logs.

maya: @alex thanks. Are there any token bucket headers in their traces? any x-burst-credits-left?

nate: I asked them for full raw request/response capture. They sent a small sample showing: 
  x-burst-credits: 0
  x-local-queue-depth: 420
  x-backend-accept-rate: 180r/s
  x-proxy-fallback: us-west-2

maya: OK that's helpful. Looks like their traffic pattern has sustained bursts that exceed the per-region commit and exhaust burst credits. But the queue depth of 420 seems high — could be a backlog in the inference pool or a routing hot spot.

oliver: Jumping in from eng-runtime: are we bumping slower autoscale in eu-west-1? Recent change to admission control in last deploy limited in-flight requests per worker to 64 (was 96). Could explain higher queueing under bursty patterns. deploy-bot: deploy 2024-11-10T03:22 rolled admission-control v1.4.

infra-ops: Hmm, I see node-level GPU utilization in eu-west-1 at 68% average but request latency distribution shows a heavy right tail at the front-end queue metric (ingress_queue_ms) ~1.1s. That implies the infra can handle tokens but the serving runtime is throttling concurrency.

maya: So two possibilities: (1) per-worker concurrency limit reduced which increases queue length, (2) routing policy's failover threshold is low causing cross-region fallback too early, creating extra latency. Which one is it?

oliver: I suspect the concurrency change. The limit was reduced to avoid OOMs for long-context models. For short requests it hurts throughput. We can test reverting admission-control for a canary pool in eu-west-1.

luis-product: Noted — product-wise we need clearer docs about concurrency impacts and defaults. But for the customer we should provide a short-term mitigation (increase burst credits or tweak routing) and a longer-term runtime fix.

alex: Immediate action items from support: (1) offer temporary regional burst credit increase for AcmeMaps for 24h, (2) suggest they add a jittered exponential backoff and prefer retrying in same region for 2 retries before fallback, (3) coordinate with eng-runtime to test canary revert.

sara-billing: I can grant a one-time 24h burst credit lift on the account. Need account id and exact window.

nate: Got account id in ticket. I'll ask for permission to toggle.

oliver: I'll spin up a canary: revert admission-control concurrency cap from 64->96 for pool eu-west-1-canary and route 5% of traffic there. Need infra-ops to approve node allocation.

infra-ops: Approve. Spinning up 4 extra nodes for canary now, will post node ids when ready.

deploy-bot: canary started eu-west-1-canary (4 nodes) - 2024-11-12T14:38:05 UTC

alex: Customer asked for repro guidance so they can validate when we change things. Suggest they run small parallel bursts of 40/80/200 requests and watch x-request-queue-time-ms and x-burst-credits. Provide script: 
```
for n in 40 80 200; do
  seq 1 $n | xargs -P$n -I{} curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}s x-queue:%{size_request}\n' -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"gpt-open-16k","prompt":"hi"}' &
  sleep 10
done
```

maya: Good. Also will add a note to the ticket that while canary runs, they may see improved latencies if routed to canary.

oliver: After 10 minutes of canary traffic we already see ingress_queue_ms median drop to 120ms and p95 drop from 1.1s->360ms for canary pool. Looks promising.

alex: I'll update the customer: we are running a targeted runtime canary to address increased queueing due to a recent concurrency cap change, we've granted them temporary burst credit, and will follow up with a permanent plan.

sara-billing: Burst credits applied for 24h window starting 2024-11-12T14:45 UTC.

nate: Customer confirmed they see p95 drop and fewer 429s when requests hit the canary. They're running additional load tests to validate.

luis-product: For follow-up: we should (a) evaluate per-model concurrency defaults, (b) expose a dashboard showing "per-region burst credit usage" to customers, (c) revisit failover thresholds so clients don't immediately get routed cross-region under short bursts.

oliver: Agreed. I'll open an internal RFC to change default admission-control policy and metrics to better surface queue saturation.

alex: Thanks everyone. I'll close this slack thread once ticket is updated. If anyone has blocking concerns about the canary or scaling, flag here. :thumbsup:
